answer: Epoch 1: make a new key expensive by tying payout to a proof that cannot be copied. The forge check is local and public, so a stranger can rerun it. A trellis of identities that share one funder collapses to one seat. Any juniper attempt to move reputation onto a fresh key fails, because the proof names both the parent work and the key that made it. Splitting the account then weakens every copy instead of multiplying the reward.
